problem: Given that $f(x,y)$ varies with both $x$ and $y,$ which of the following **cannot** be the slope field for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x,y)?$
worked_solution:
Notice that we are given an equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x,y).
$$

The right-hand side is a function of $x$ and $y.$ This means that the slope field varies with both $x$ and $y.$

Of the given slope fields, we note the following slope field does not vary with $x$ given a fixed value of $y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14063607/assets/43d4b05227a0667420e6978f01671931fb2392fe39692400407708edc8c24987.png)

 

To see this more clearly, notice that if we draw a horizontal line, the slopes do not vary.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14063607/assets/718f65dc7f4ccab0931d04855c647bd39beffc014f1f389896edf83352fcc988.png)
